finding_2_where_the_blueprint_stops_bein: Swept across budgets on the inspect lane. The corpus as built delivers the blueprint within the 5-pt bound to ~55.4B (55B=4.3801 PASS, 56B=5.5020 FAIL) and to ~56.9B with everyday-conversations dropped (55B=1.7422 PASS, 57B=5.0108 FAIL). The released run's 59.9B is past both, at 11.4593. Below the knee the whole 3.99 pts is everyday-conversations -- 403,573 tokens cannot fund a 2% share -- and dropping it gives EXACTLY 0.0000 at 30B and at 50B. Above the knee the same removal buys ~1.5B of budget. The knee sits just above the headroom curve's 53.8B stack-edu-python ceiling and is the same fact: the freed 2% renormalizes onto sources already at the cap, so past it the constraint is supply, not a removable source.
the_trap_the_gate_is_built_around: l1_skew_pts sees ONE of cap_weights_by_epochs's two failure modes. When the cap binds it reweights and skew rises. When no allocation satisfies the cap at all, targets come back unchanged and the skew is 0.00 BY CONSTRUCTION -- its best possible value at the one budget where repetition is bounded by nothing. So mixture_skew_verdict carries the fallback guard, using train.py's own discriminator (after a successful cap nothing exceeds the limit, so max_epochs_seen > max_epochs is true precisely in the unbounded case). runs/corpus/phase7-gate-as-built.json is that guard firing on real data: 2,968 epochs, skew 0.0000, refused.
the_defect_i_shipped_and_repaired_in_the: The first run of this gate reported fineweb-edu at 46.9 epochs and EVERY source over the cap at 59.9B. Cause: it counted data/shards/<src>/total_tokens, which on this box is a FETCH -- 479M of fineweb-edu's 5.19B -- and the manifests say so in subset_of. Counting local files understates supply 10x-30x. source_supply() now defaults to subset_of.total_tokens, records per source which figure it used, and --local-supply asks the other question deliberately. Three regression tests. Anything on this box that reads total_tokens to reason about corpus supply has the same bug.
